articles.title: Christopher Kane and Mulberry make swaggering joint comeback at London fashion week
articles.summary: Appointment of Kane as creative director signals the return of serious style ambition for former It-bag brand. With spicy leather mini-dresses and shoes with miniature axes for heels, two beloved British names made a swaggering joint comeback at London fashion week.
body: Fifteen years ago, Christopher Kane and Mulberry were two of the biggest shows on the line-up. Kane was the brilliant young designer who could find fashion in the most unlikely places: rubberised lace minis were inspired by “Princess Margaret on acid”; while illustrations from the 1972 classic The Joy of Sex appeared on slinky slip dresses. Mulberry was London’s home-grown It-bag brand: anyone who was anyone had a Bayswater or an Alexa.

On paper, it is an unlikely match. Mulberry is rooted in its Somerset factories and makes understated practical bags; Kane has a flair for bad-girl party dresses learned on the streets of Glasgow where he grew up.

Where they meet is leather. There were leather sheath dresses and elegantly spare leather car coats, as well as heeled loafers featuring Mulberry’s signature postman’s lock. Kane builds each collection around one visual motif – Frankenstein, gorillas, the reproductive organs of plants – and for this collection, took the castellated leather flaps of Mulberry’s Bayswater bags and turned them into notched hems and necklines. This was punchy, full-throttle fashion, accessorised with money-making bags and shoes.
points: Appointment of Kane as creative director signals the return of serious style ambition for former It-bag brand.

articles.title: Hollywood’s Big Night Out: Inside the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art’s Star-Studded Grand Reveal
articles.summary: On Saturday night, ahead of its September 22 opening, the museum drew a star-studded crowd of Hollywood’s biggest names, from Harrison Ford and Steven Spielberg to Leonardo DiCaprio, Oprah Winfrey, Michael B. Jordan, Katy Perry, and Kim Kardashian.
body: Founded by filmmaker George Lucas and his wife, Mellody Hobson, the museum is not simply a monument to Star Wars, but a sweeping love letter to the art of storytelling, bringing together paintings, illustrations, photography, animation and cinematic imagery that explore how pictures have the power to shape the stories we tell.

Located in downtown Los Angeles, across from Lucas’s alma mater, the University of Southern California, the museum is a five-story, 300,000-square-foot building featuring 35 galleries and more than 40,000 works. The collection spans celebrated artists including Norman Rockwell, Frida Kahlo, and Banksy, as well as comic art by Jack Kirby. And yes, there are plenty of Star Wars artifacts. The museum’s inaugural exhibition, Star Wars in Motion, showcases vehicles, costumes—including Princess Leia’s—props, and artwork from the first six films. There’s also Luke Skywalker’s Landspeeder and the first physical build of General Grievous’s Wheel Bike from Revenge of the Sith.

articles.title: Victoria Starmer models clothes at London fashion week show
articles.summary: Wife of former PM takes part in designer Edeline Lee’s show inspired by the Greek myth of Sisyphus. Victoria Starmer has taken part in a London fashion week show, in one of her first public appearances since her husband, Keir Starmer, stepped down as prime minister.
body: Lady Starmer appeared at Sunday’s Edeline Lee show. The London-based, Canadian British designer’s clothes are a favourite of the Princess of Wales, and have also been worn by celebrities including singer Taylor Swift and actor and screenwriter Phoebe Waller-Bridge.

Lee’s spring/summer 2027 show took place in the unusual setting of a north London school sports hall. Starmer wore a bright turquoise knitted midi dress with a high neckline, pleated detailing and short, sculptural sleeves, paired with white block-heeled shoes, with her hair worn in loose waves.

Rather than preparations for the show taking place backstage in the usual way, in Lee’s unique show, models were fitted and adjusted in full view of the audience, dancers rehearsed beside the catwalk, while a drone followed proceedings from the high ceiling of the gymnasium.

Starmer was photographed having her makeup done beside the catwalk, against a backdrop of a football net, with makeup and hair products spread out over a table in front of her. Ballerinas stretched beside the catwalk and synchronised swimming-inspired dancers performed in bright red costumes as part of the show, in the school in Chalk Farm.

articles.title: Hungry for connection? This is what we lose when we stop eating together | Shadi Khan Saif
articles.summary: Mealtimes offer a pause in the day for parents and children to sit together, listen to one another and trade stories. Making sense of it is a column about spirituality and how it can be used to navigate everyday life. When I was growing up in a Muslim household, food was rarely just food.
body: There was even a small ritual around something as ordinary as a piece of bread. If it fell on the ground anywhere in the house or was even seen on the ground outside, we would pick it up, clean it, kiss it respectfully and place it somewhere clean and safe. Food was not to be treated carelessly.
And sending a guest away without offering them a meal is unthinkable – almost a sin.
As a child, I didn’t think of any of this as “spirituality”. It was simply what you did. Eating alone felt like punishment. It still does.

Only later, after leaving Afghanistan and building a life in Australia, did I begin to understand what those ordinary habits carried with them: gratitude, hospitality and a sense that food was something to be celebrated – and shared.

articles.title: Kim Kardashian and Lewis Hamilton Have Found Their Loved-up Couple Style Rhythm
articles.summary: From Lake Como to London, the couple quickly found their style sensibilities overlap often. An appearance at the Lucas Museum proved it’s red carpet-worthy.
body: Kim Kardashian and Lewis Hamilton have been taking their romance across the globe: from boating on Lake Como to riding Lime Bikes in London and witnessing history at Celine Dion’s Paris residency show. Their latest appearance, at the Lucas Museum Of Narrative Art’s opening night in Los Angeles, marked a major moment for the loved-up couple.

Having just returned from London where she was celebrating her Skims flagship store opening, Kardashian zipped back across the pond to support her F1 driver boyfriend as he served as an evening co-chair for the grand opening celebration. She opted for a shimmering black and floral embroidered Saint Laurent by Tom Ford fall 2004 dress with a mint underlining, paired with Oscar Heyman earrings and a Zydo ring. It was a look that hit all the Kim Kardashian style pressure points: sparkly, skin-tight, super glam.
Makeup and hair followed a similar beat, with her hair slicked back into a bun, chiseled and warm contour, and siren-like eyes.

An appearance at the Lucas Museum proved it’s red carpet-worthy.

articles.title: From the Archives: Inside Stefano Gabbana and Domenico Dolce’s Glamorous Milan Apartment
articles.summary: In a Milan triplex, Stefano Gabbana and Domenico Dolce have created an environment as glamorous—and leopard-laden—as their fashion. Hamish Bowles drops in on their dolce vita.
body: “Animal Magnetism,” by Hamish Bowles, was originally published in the May 2000 issue of Vogue.
As their glamorous new Milanese penthouse bears witness, designers Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana are as much mix-masters at home as they are on the runways.

IN THE SWIM The designers' signature leopard print even shows up poolside. The triplex penthouse is perched high above the Milan skyline, with landscaped terraces. The pool is made of volcanic-rock tiles from Stromboli.

For their production this season, the sweeping chords of Pietro Mascagni’s Cavalleria Rusticana (“sweet and strong and romantic”) opened the show, as they have done for thirteen years, only to segue symbolically into poundingly high-voltage disco. In the designers’ new aerie, centuries also collide, and gilded eighteenth- and nineteenth-century furnishings sit comfortably beneath Basquiats and Warhols.
points: In a Milan triplex, Stefano Gabbana and Domenico Dolce have created an environment as glamorous—and leopard-laden—as their fashion.

articles.title: Perfect Fit: Kim Kardashian Celebrates Skims’s First International Flagship in London
articles.summary: London came calling, and Central Cee, Troye Sivan, and Kim Petras joined in on the fun amid fashion week.
body: Body-ody-ody had been the sentiment of London Fashion Week, with designers playing with all things sexy on the runways. And on Friday night, the city got to take that further and indulge in the Skims treatment, as co-founders Kim Kardashian and Jens Grede welcomed friends of the brand to its newly opened Regent Street flagship —the first international standalone store for the shapewear and intimates behemoth.

It was Kardashian’s first time visiting the London store, following its soft opening in July. Naturally, she dressed for the occasion. She wore Ludovic de Saint Sernin’s Mermaid Bi Dress in flesh-toned leather, which closely contoured her curves with a grommet-studded bodice and lace-up slit revealing a sheer underlay beneath. The choice was particularly apt: Kardashian’s forthcoming collaboration with the designer is set to launch October 1, marrying Skims’s shapewear foundations with Saint Sernin’s unapologetically sexy, party-ready signatures. Later, she shimmied into a sculpted chocolate brown corset with belted and tie-up detailing and a hip-skimming maxi skirt.
